# Activation Functions

A reusable executable function definition for managing a document’s participant roster, reviewed terms, acceptance and access readiness. It operates on `/activation`, reads configuration from `/clauses/activation/parameters`, and creates participant channels and operations under `/contracts`. All paths refer to the document executing the functions, including when that document is nested.

## State and access

`parties` maps role names to party data. Each party supplies `lead/channel`; additional `representatives` supply their own `channel`. Lead channels use the role name, while representative channels use `<role>__<repId>`. Party and representative names must be nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`.

`required` identifies parties whose acceptance is needed; `approved` records acceptance by role. `revision` identifies the Activation revision reviewed by approval and admission operations. `frozen` prevents roster changes; `closed` prevents activation. Neither is set by the functions shown here.

`accessPaths` identifies embedded Timeline Access documents. `readers` supplies named groups of alternative reader keys. `readerGroups` adds each party’s `readerKeys` and each additional representative’s `readerKeys`, replacing any same-named configured group.

`accessValid` checks every lead and representative transport. External Channel instances bypass its Timeline Access check. Other transports must be Timeline Channels. For each such timeline, at least one access document must match its provider, contain that exact timeline in `allowedTimelines`, and contain at least one key from **every** reader group in `allowedKeys`. Different documents cannot collectively satisfy the groups for one timeline under this check. An empty group cannot satisfy it.

`computeState` also includes proposed parties from `accessRequests` whose `expectedRevision` matches the current `revision` when checking access. Thus a pending admission can affect readiness before changing `parties`. It derives:

- `accessReady` and `functional`: the access-check result.
- `termsAccepted`: every role in `required` is approved and every stored `terms/fields` value still equals the corresponding document field.
- `active`: access is ready, terms are accepted and `closed` is not true.
- `status`: `CLOSED` takes precedence; otherwise access failure gives `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` before any activation or `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` afterward; ready access gives `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` or `ACTIVE`.
- `reason`: `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING` takes precedence over `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`; otherwise it is empty. It does not independently explain closure.

These checks use empty collections for missing roster, reader, access-request, required-party and approval collections, and false for missing approval and relevant flag checks. Those execution fallbacks do not make an absent stored result a confirmed false value. In particular, an empty `required` list imposes no party-approval requirement, but terms and access checks still apply.

## Terms and approval

`initializeTerms` leaves existing `/activation/terms` unchanged. Otherwise it uses `/clauseRuntime/initialDocument` to establish `terms/definition` and captures the current values at `negotiation/allowedPaths` into `terms/fields`. `allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`; each configured field must exist and be text, integer, double or boolean. Missing or nonscalar fields reject initialization.

The definition reference excludes those negotiated fields, content at `accessPaths`, Activation parameter fields `accessPaths` and `readers`, and configured parties’ top-level `readerKeys`. `terms/ref` identifies the resulting definition-and-fields record. Initialization sets `termsRevision` and `negotiation/revision` to `1`, `negotiation/editable` to true, and `history`, `outcomes` and `proposal` to empty objects. `termsCurrent` checks the captured fields against current values; it does not recompare the entire initial document.

`approve(input)` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be true, `call/channel` to name a current party’s lead role, and integer `input.revision` to match `/activation/revision`. It also requires valid participant access. With nonempty `negotiation/allowedPaths`, text `termsRef` is required; whenever supplied, it must equal `/activation/terms/ref`. Failures include `EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `ONLY_PARTY_LEAD_CAN_ACCEPT`, `STALE_TERMS_REVISION`, `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `TERMS_REFERENCE_REQUIRED` and `TERMS_CHANGED`.

After those checks, an already-approved party returns true without another event. A new approval records `approved[call/channel] = true`, commits state and emits `Terms Accepted` with `party` and `revision`. If that commit returns active, any pending negotiation proposal is recorded in `history` with outcome `SUPERSEDED`, cleared, and `negotiation/editable` becomes false. A true approval return means that party’s approval was accepted, not necessarily that the document became active. `approveWithTerms` exposes the revision-and-terms-reference input and delegates to `approve`.

## Roster changes and admission

`updatePartyPublic` accepts `replacement` and optional `party`, removes the input’s type marker and delegates to `updateParty`. The target defaults to `call/channel`; no input revision is required. Exact-document review is still mandatory. The invoking channel must be an existing party lead, the roster must not be frozen, and an existing party cannot manage another existing party. Adding an explicit new role requires `allowNewParties`, whose check defaults to false.

`replacement` replaces the party data and must contain `lead/channel`; additional representative names are validated. The resulting roster must pass access validation. Generated contract names must not collide with contracts outside the previous roster’s contributions. Success installs the resulting contracts, clears all `approved` entries, adds a newly created role to `required`, increments `revision`, commits state and emits `Party Changed`. Even an unchanged replacement follows this update path. The revision increment uses `1` as its fallback when the prior revision is absent.

`admitApprovedParties(input)` is a separate admission path. It rejects a frozen roster, mismatched `expectedRevision`, or an empty configured `admission/approvers` list, which defaults to `[]`. The function itself does not collect or verify those approvers’ votes; its caller must establish the approved-admission context.

`input.parties` defaults to `{}`. Each supplied role must be valid and each party must have a lead channel and a nonempty, duplicate-free list of nonempty text `readerKeys`. An existing role must have the same lead-channel identity and the same primary reader-key set, regardless of ordering; its existing party data is retained. Access must validate for the resulting roster. An unchanged roster returns `outcome: duplicate` after these checks.

For a changed roster, `runtimeDefinition` supplies generated operation implementations. Contract conflicts reject admission; otherwise channels are installed before handlers, `revision` increments, and state is committed. `required` is not extended by this path. It emits `Party Changed` for every supplied role, including retained roles, with `kind: Participants admitted`, `admissionRef` and the new revision, then returns `outcome: acceptedNew`.

Whenever `commitState` detects changed `parties` or `required` and prior terms exist, it updates the terms definition/reference and increments `termsRevision`. Any pending negotiation proposal becomes `AUTHORITY_CHANGED` in `outcomes`, is recorded in `history`, and is cleared. Approvals are cleared here when negotiation has nonempty `allowedPaths`; without that configuration they are preserved unless the calling operation already cleared them.

## Access requests and installation

`requestPartyAddition` reads the current event, including `admissionRef`, `expectedRevision`, `parties`, `accessDocuments`, `clauseKey` and `itemPath`. It silently ignores stale revisions and previously stored admission references. It validates supplied access documents against the proposed parties’ transports and installs any supplied documents under `/partyAccess`.

Using reader groups for the combined current and proposed roster, it checks each **existing** party’s transports. For each party lacking access, it emits `Party Access Update Requested` and stores a request under `/activation/accessRequests/<admissionRef>/requests/<party>`. The request carries the party’s lead `channel`, `readerGroups`, correlation fields, `accessPath` of `/timelineAccess/<party>`, `expectedAccessEntry` identifying the current provider checkpoint event or an empty string if absent, and `ready: false`. The admission record also stores the proposed `parties` and `expectedRevision`; it does not admit them.

`refreshAccessRequests` updates stored request `ready` values only for the current Activation revision, using the current party and access documents with the request’s saved reader groups. Readiness does not itself establish admission or provider ownership authority.

Inherited `installTimelineAccess` accepts between 1 and 16 documents per invocation. Each must be an initialized Timeline Access document with provider checkpoint history and the expected provider-channel update policy preserved in both its original and current contracts. Documents are deduplicated by original-document identity. New documents are referenced beneath `basePath`, added to `accessPaths`, and given embedded channels and refresh workflows using `/contracts/activationInitializedRefresh/steps`; channel names are recorded in `registeredAccessChannels`. It returns `duplicate` or `acceptedNew`.

## Commit, channels and inherited helpers

`refresh` initializes terms if needed, commits derived state, then refreshes access requests. `commitState` maintains `everActivated`, emits `Document Activated` on first activation, `Document Access Suspended` when a previously active document loses access, and `Document Access Restored` when an already-activated document becomes active after previously lacking access. These events carry `revision`; restoration of access alone does not emit restoration while acceptance or closure still prevents activation.

Until `channelsInstalled` is true, `reconcileInitialChannels` installs empty Composite External Channels while access is unready and actual transports when ready. Conflicting existing contracts reject installation. When ready, it sets `channelsInstalled` and, if the execution supplies `timestamp`, records `channelsAdmittedAfter`. Later access loss does not uninstall channels through this function.

`rosterContracts` generates transports plus `approve_<role>` and `updateParty_<role>` operations bound to each lead role. Requests come from `call/request`; approval uses `approveWithTerms` when negotiation paths are configured. Listing additional representatives does not grant them these lead-only operations.

Inherited `requireActive` checks stored activation and current roster access, and optionally current representative authority for workflows. `businessReady` independently checks closure, required approvals, current terms and roster access. Both permit documents without `/activation`; neither includes pending-admission parties in its own access check.

Inherited party-mapping helpers resolve explicit role mappings, validate declared party specializations and preserve every configuring party’s main channel/key identity. Mapping grants neither access nor consent. Inherited amendment helpers use supplied `bindings.state` and `bindings.editable`, `parameters.paths` and `parameters.approvers`: proposals require the expected revision, an allowed path and editable terms; approval requires a listed approver and the current proposal. All configured approvals apply the replacement, advance amendment revision, record history, clear the proposal and emit `Amendment Applied`. Recording or partially approving a proposal is not application; duplicate outcomes do not repeat it.

These functions do not perform provider permission changes. Access requests are intentions; confirmed provider history and completed document execution establish permissions and outcomes.
